sections.title: Distance and Section Formulas
sections.content: Distance between (x1,y1) and (x2,y2) is √[(x2-x1)² + (y2-y1)²]. The section formula finds a point dividing a segment in ratio m:n. Internally: [(mx2+nx1)/(m+n), (my2+ny1)/(m+n)]. Externally: change '+' to '-'.

sections.title: Centers of a Triangle
sections.content: Centroid (G) divides medians in 2:1. Coordinates: [(x1+x2+x3)/3, (y1+y2+y3)/3]. Incenter (I) coordinates: [(ax1+bx2+cx3)/(a+b+c), (ay1+by2+cy3)/(a+b+c)] where a,b,c are side lengths.

sections.title: Slope and Forms of a Line
sections.content: Slope m = tanθ = (y2-y1)/(x2-x1). Line equations: 1) Point-Slope: y-y1 = m(x-x1). 2) Slope-Intercept: y = mx+c. 3) Two-Point: y-y1 = [(y2-y1)/(x2-x1)](x-x1). 4) Intercept form: x/a + y/b = 1.

sections.title: Angle Between Two Lines
sections.content: If two lines have slopes m1 and m2, the acute angle θ between them is given by tanθ = |(m1 - m2) / (1 + m1*m2)|. Lines are parallel if m1 = m2, and perpendicular if m1*m2 = -1.

sections.title: Standard and General Equation of a Circle
sections.content: Standard: (x-h)² + (y-k)² = r² with center (h,k) and radius r. General: x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0. Center is (-g, -f) and radius is √(g² + f² - c).

sections.title: Position of a Point w.r.t Circle
sections.content: Substitute the point (x1, y1) into the circle's equation (let it be S). S1 = x1² + y1² + 2gx1 + 2fy1 + c. If S1 > 0 (Outside), S1 = 0 (On circle), S1 < 0 (Inside).

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1) Forgetting that in the general circle equation, coefficients of x² and y² must be exactly 1 before finding center/radius.
2) Confusing internal and external section formula signs.
3) Dividing by zero when calculating slope for vertical lines.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 1 establishes the coordinate plane basics. Master finding slopes, writing basic line equations, extracting centers/radii from circle equations, and checking point positions.

tricks.title: Collinearity Check Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Three points are collinear if the slope between the first two equals the slope between the last two. (y2-y1)/(x2-x1) = (y3-y2)/(x3-x2).

tricks.title: Parallel Line Shortcut
tricks.explanation: A line parallel to ax + by + c = 0 will always be of the form ax + by + k = 0. Just find 'k' using the given point.
tricks.example: Parallel to 2x+3y-5=0 passing through (1,1) → 2(1)+3(1)+k=0 → k=-5. Line: 2x+3y-5=0.

tricks.title: Perpendicular Line Shortcut
tricks.explanation: A line perpendicular to ax + by + c = 0 is bx - ay + k = 0. Swap the x and y coefficients and flip one sign.

tricks.title: Quick Center and Radius
tricks.explanation: From x² + y² + Dx + Ey + F = 0, Center is (-D/2, -E/2). Radius is √(Center_x² + Center_y² - F).

tricks.title: Shoelace Method for Polygon Area
tricks.explanation: Write coordinates in a column, repeating the first point at the end. Multiply diagonally down (add) and diagonally up (subtract), then halve the absolute result.

tricks.title: Intercepts of a Circle Shortcut
tricks.explanation: X-intercept length = 2√(g²-c). Y-intercept length = 2√(f²-c). If g²=c, it touches the X-axis.
